svg.aria-label: The stats screen and where its figures come from. In total: 78 encounters in 2026 against 33 in 2025, or +136%, with 18 people each counted once. Top rated: the average score, halved to fit out of five, then the number of times; Noa J. at 4.9, Gabriel T. and Ibrahim D. at 4.8, split by the exact average; the podium covers every year. What it brought in: €750 over 7 paid nights out of 78, or €107.14 on average, the average only counting paid nights. By month: each encounter in its month, September first with 18 times. Breakdown: 18 cards sorted by role, 8 versatile, 6 top, 4 bottom, counted in people, not encounters. Everything is computed in SQL inside the encrypted database.

svg.text: Five figures for the chosen year, all computed in the database, from your encounters.

g.text: over 7 nights, out of the year’s 78
On the cards where the role is filled in.
The 18 people: COUNT(DISTINCT personne_id), each counted once.
An empty year before? No percentage: dividing by zero says nothing.
TOP RATED: AN AVERAGE, THEN A SORT
AVG(note) ORDER BY moyenne DESC, nb DESC LIMIT 3
Scores are half-points out of ten: the average halved gives 4.9.
Gabriel and Ibrahim both show 4.8. The exact average, before rounding,
is what separates them, ahead of Ibrahim’s 10 times.
Across all years: switching year leaves the podium as it is.
WHAT IT BROUGHT IN: A SUM, AN AVERAGE
The 78 nights of 2026, 7 of them with an amount
The average only counts paid nights: the others, where the question
never came up, would drag it down.
The gold bar is 7 out of 78: you see whether it is often or rare.
+36% on 2025. Had 2025 brought in nothing, there would be no percentage.
BY MONTH: EACH ENCOUNTER IN ITS MONTH
The busiest reads “September · 18 times”. Without the word “times”,
it read like a date: 18 September.
Twelve integers come back from the database, not seventy-eight encounters.
SELECT role, COUNT(*) FROM personnes GROUP BY role
Counted in people: the question is “who with”, not “how many times”.
Every card where the role is filled in, whatever the year.

svg.text: COUNT, SUM and AVG in SQL: no need to
haul every encounter into the app.
Total, earnings, months: the chosen year.
The figures come from the sample data, the same as in the screenshots.
